Export data to CSV

Source: R/export.R
export_csv.Rd

Save a data.frame to a CSV file on disk. This function automatically handles creation of the target directory, appends the .csv extension if needed, and chooses an appropriate writer based on the column separator.

Usage

export_csv(
  data,
  path = "exports",
  filename = "cleaned_data",
  sep = ";",
  row.names = FALSE,
  overwrite = TRUE,
  verbose = TRUE
)

Arguments

data

The data.frame to export.

path

Destination folder path (default "exports"). The folder will be created if it does not exist.

filename

File name. The .csv extension is added automatically if necessary (default "cleaned_data").

sep

Column separator character (default ";").

row.names

Logical. Should row names be included in the file? (default FALSE).

overwrite

Logical. If FALSE, an error is thrown if the file already exists. If TRUE (default), it is overwritten.

verbose

Logical. If TRUE (default), prints a message with the full path of the written file.

Value

(Invisibly) returns the full path to the created file.

Details

The function simplifies CSV export by performing the following steps:

  1. Check that the data object is a data.frame.

  2. Create the path directory recursively if it does not already exist.

  3. Append the .csv extension to the file name if it is missing.

  4. Choose an optimised writing function based on the separator:

    • For sep = ";": use utils::write.csv2 (European-style format).

    • For sep = ",": use utils::write.csv (US-style format).

    • Otherwise: use utils::write.table.

See also

Other Export functions: write_cleaning_report()

Examples

# Test data
df_test <- data.frame(
  id = 1:3,
  name = c("Alice", "Bob", "Charlie"),
  score = c(10.5, 15.2, 8.0)
)

# Create a temporary folder to avoid writing on your disk
tmp_folder <- tempfile() # Use a random folder name

# 1. Simple export (semicolon separator by default)
path_file <- export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export")
#> Error in export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export"): could not find function "export_csv"

# Check that the file exists
file.exists(path_file)
#> Error: object 'path_file' not found

# 2. Export with comma separator and no overwrite (should error if rerun)
try({
  export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export", sep = ",", overwrite = FALSE)
})
#> Error in export_csv(df_test, path = tmp_folder, filename = "test_export",  : 
#>   could not find function "export_csv"

# Clean up temporary folder
unlink(tmp_folder, recursive = TRUE)
